new_statements.quote: Karena dalam BBK tekanan kata tidak bersifat fonemik, maka ia tidak direalisir dalam bentuk ortografi. [...] Tekanan yang teratur ini umumnya jatuh pada suku kedua dari belakang: /banyu/ [bányu] 'air', /kaka/ [káka] 'kakak', /pulun/ [púlun] 'bungkus'. Tekanan kata dapat berubah atau bertukar tempat dari suku kedua dari belakang ke lain suku berdasarkan kondisi-kondisi sebagai berikut. (1) Tekanan akan jatuh pada suku terakhir pada kata yang suku terakhirnya berintikan diftong /aw/, /ay/, /uy/ [...] (2) Bagi suku kedua dari belakang yang berintikan vokal /ə/, tekanan akan berpindah pada suku akhir. new_statements.translation: Because word stress in Banjar Kuala is not phonemic, it is not represented in the orthography. [...] This regular stress generally falls on the second syllable from the end: /banyu/ [bányu] 'water', /kaka/ [káka] 'elder sibling', /pulun/ [púlun] 'wrap'. Word stress can change or move from the penultimate syllable to another syllable under the following conditions. (1) Stress falls on the last syllable in words whose last syllable has the diphthong /aw/, /ay/, /uy/ as nucleus [...] (2) When the penultimate syllable has the vowel /ə/ as nucleus, stress moves to the final syllable. [...] (3) When the first syllable of a disyllabic word consists of a single vowel only (VCV(C) structure), stress falls on the second (last) syllable.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is non-contrastive and by default penultimate. It is final instead when (1) the final syllable contains a diphthong aw/ay/uy ([babáw], [lulúy]), (2) the penult vowel is schwa ([bətám], [kəntóŋ]), or (3) a disyllable begins with an onsetless V syllable ([idúp], [umíh]); in CVV.CV(C) words with a vowel sequence it may be antepenultimate or penultimate.. actually penult-of-sequence or final ([kúini]~[kuiní], [búaya]~[buayá]). Morphology: suffixes -an, -i, -(a)kan often pull stress onto the suffix syllable ([bálum] > [balumán]); possessive enclitics -ku, -nya are always stressed when word-final ([rúmah] > [rumahkú]). In phrases the stress shifts to the following word ([rúmah], [rumah gánal], [rumah nan gánal]).
new_statements.exceptions: Final stress with final diphthongs, schwa penults, VCV(C) disyllables; free variation in CVVCV(C) words; 'irregular' (morphologically conditioned) final stress with suffixes -an/-i/-(a)kan and obligatory stress on final possessive enclitics -ku/-nya.
new_statements.domain_note: Explicitly distinguishes word stress (3.3.1.1, citation forms) from phrase stress (3.3.1.2), where the prominence moves to the last word of the phrase - suggesting the 'word stress' observed may be phrase-final prominence on isolated words. Stress stated to be non-phonemic; impressionistic description, no measurements.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes Bahasa Banjar Kuala (BBK), the Kuala dialect spoken around Banjarmasin/Martapura/Pelaihari, which (per the source and Adelaar 1992 fn. 33) differs from Banjar Hulu mainly in having schwa/mid vowels; Glottolog banj1239 covers both Hulu and Kuala (no separate dialect glottocodes known to me). The Banjar Hulu descriptions (Durasid & Kawi 1978; Adelaar 1992) only say stress is non-phonemic. Glottolog also files Poerwadi et al. 1993 'Fonologi bahasa Tamuan' under banj1239, but Tamuan is a Central Kalimantan (Kotawaringin) Malayic variety and was not obtained.

sources.note: Sec. 3.3.1 pp. 38-40: word stress not phonemic; regular stress on the penult ([bányu], [káka], [púlun]); shifts to the final syllable when the final has diphthong /aw, ay, uy/, when the penult nucleus is /ə/, in VCV(C) disyllables ([idúp]); penult or antepenult in CVVCV(C) ([kúini]~[kuiní]); suffixes -an/-i/-(a)kan often and possessive enclitics -ku/-nya always draw stress to the final; in phrases stress moves to the following word ([rúmah] vs [rumah gánal]).
